title: Comparing sizes: cardinality, Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein, and diagonal arguments
summary: Compare sets by injections and bijections, construct the Cantor–Schröder–Bernstein bijection, and use diagonal arguments to prove uncountability and the strict growth of power sets.
abstract: Pairing elements one to one lets us compare the sizes of sets, even when counting never ends. In this setting, an infinite set can have the same size as a proper part of itself. Matching the elements of each of two sets to distinct elements of the other is also enough to guarantee equal size. Yet infinite sets are not all equally large: the real numbers cannot be listed by the natural numbers, and the collection of all subsets of any set is strictly larger than that set.
